title: okl intake pr <n>: a PR's resolved review findings, put to the encoding loop (#376)

issues.title: okl intake pr <n>: bring a PR's resolved review findings into the encoding loop
issues.body:
## Where it stands (main, 24784b4)
The Stop hook is the only mechanical intake: it asks what the session itself learned. A finding made anywhere else reaches the store only when an agent records it by hand. That includes a PR's review threads, a CI failure and a live check run against a deployed system. In one consumer repo this week:
- seven review comments on one PR held two real regressions;
- a live container check on another PR found a case-insensitive match reopening routes that config meant to close.

Both reached okl only because the session agent recorded them by hand. A PR that no session opens is never asked.

## Proposal
`okl intake pr <n>` lists the PR's resolved review threads and the commits that resolved them (through `gh`). For each it asks the encoding-loop question: encode it or not, at which surface (test, CI, rule, lesson), and if not, why not. It prints the `okl record` and `okl verify` commands for the ones to encode. Optionally, a CI job comments on a merged PR with the findings no lesson covers.

## Tests
- Against a fixture of a PR's threads (recorded `gh` JSON, no network), it lists each resolved thread with its resolving commit.
- Unresolved threads are left out.
- The printed commands are ones the CLI accepts.

Related: #97 (a candidate inbox), #190 (a one-off review of past CodeRabbit findings).

title: Give CI a store: a committed drift snapshot

issues.title: Give CI a store: a committed drift snapshot
issues.body:
## Problem
This repo's CI has no knowledge store, so the `okl-verify` drift step runs, checks nothing and warns "Drift not checked" (#21 made that honest, but it is still unchecked). The same is true for any consumer without a hosted service, and for every fork PR, which gets no secrets.

The obvious fix — commit the rules and `okl seed` them in CI — produces a false all-clear: seeding goes through `record()`, which stamps `verified_at` fresh, so every rule looks just-verified and nothing ever drifts.

## Plan
- `okl export --drift` writes `okl-drift.json`: the in-scope rules that govern files (`id`, `title`, `scope`, `files`, `verified_at`, `verified_by`), sorted, no bodies, no generated timestamp (stable diffs).
- `okl drift --snapshot okl-drift.json` reads the **committed** snapshot (`git show HEAD:`), not the working tree, and builds nodes in memory — no store, no `record()`, real timestamps.
- The snapshot is refused (exit 2) when an entry's `verified_at` falls outside the window around the minute stamped in its `verified_by` evidence (one minute before to five after, for clock skew) — a hand-edited timestamp does not clear drift. A deliberate forgery of both fields is still possible; it shows in the PR diff, where review is the guard.
- `okl verify` refreshes the snapshot when one exists, so re-verifying and updating CI's view is one step.
- `okl-verify.yml` (all three mirrors) uses the snapshot when no service is configured and the file is tracked.
- Drift's advice line stops recommending `okl record --verified` (which CLAUDE.md bans) and names `okl verify`.

A hosted service (#26 territory) stays compatible: `OKL_SERVICE_URL` still wins when set.

lesson_text:
[n_e7988ff536fb] Rule · Exit codes are this CLI's public API: 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 refused
symptom: a new command, or a new error path in an existing one, that returns 0 or 1 on a condition meaning 'this did not run'
fix: return 2 and print the reason to stderr; add a test asserting the code and that stdout stayed empty
body: cause: okl runs inside other people's hooks and CI, where the exit code is the only thing read. 0 means the check ran and found nothing; 1 means it ran and found something (drift, duplicates); 2 means it could not run at all — unconfigured, unreachable, rejected credentials, invalid input. Collapsing 2 into 0 is the silence-as-safety failure the whole tool exists to prevent, and collapsing it into 1 makes a misconfiguration look like a finding.
defect: A malformed okl-drift.json (rules a string, or an entry that is not a dict) raises a traceback (exit 1, which --gate reads as drift found).
fix: Refuse a malformed snapshot with exit 2.

title: doctor, init and metric say what the interests hide (#374)

issues.title: A repo set up before a default interest never gets it, and nothing says how many lessons its interests hide
issues.body:
## Where it stands (main, 24784b4, 2026-11-06)
- `_init_interests` (`src/okl/cli/install.py:613`) only fills an empty interest list. That is deliberate since #340: a re-run never overrides a list someone chose. Detection has since added `security` and `method`, because the portable lessons are filed under them. A repo configured before that change keeps its narrower list through every upgrade.
- `core._in_scope` (`src/okl/core.py:49`) hides every org lesson whose subjects are outside the list. One consumer repo was configured in July with five interests and neither of those two. In it, 26 of 70 org lessons never reached a briefing, among them the authorization-test and IDOR lessons.
- `okl metric` reported "42 of 45 never shown". Its denominator, "lessons this repo can be briefed", already leaves the hidden ones out (`core.exposure_report` counts only what `_in_scope` passes). So the report never mentioned the other 26, and nobody looked.

## Proposal
1. `okl doctor` and a re-run of `okl init` report how many org lessons the interests hide. They name the default subjects the config lacks, with the command that adds them. Neither changes the list, so #340's rule stands.
2. `okl metric` reports the count the interests hide, beside the lessons this repo can be briefed.

## Tests
- A store holds an org lesson tagged only `security`, and the config lacks `security`. `okl doctor` names the lesson and the missing subject.
- A re-run of `okl init` prints the offer and leaves `interests` unchanged.
- `okl metric` counts that lesson as hidden by interests.

Related: #340, #91.

lesson_text:
[n_02cc84da158d] Defect · OKL_DATABASE_URL was honoured by the store and ignored by every CLI command
symptom: a documented storage env var works in one entry point and is silently overridden in another; writes land somewhere other than where the operator pointed them
fix: resolve the storage target in ONE place that every entry point calls; if a component deliberately ignores the variable, refuse loudly rather than silently substituting a default
body: cause: Store honoured OKL_DATABASE_URL from v0.1 and the HTTP service passed it through, but Client._local_store built a config-adjacent sqlite URL unconditionally - so every CLI command ignored it. Pointing the variable at Postgres and running okl record reported success and wrote to a local file. Found while building a diagram generator that needed a scratch store: the seed step printed 'seeded 10 records' and the target database was empty, which is the exit-0-with-no-output case the verify_materialized gate exists for. The variable was never unsupported; it was supported in the layer nobody entered through.
defect: cli/health.py::_no_store_yet re-reads OKL_DATABASE_URL with `is None`, but the client treats an empty value as unset, so with OKL_DATABASE_URL="" okl doctor creates .okl/okl.db.
fix: Treat an empty OKL_DATABASE_URL as unset.

title: check: a relevance floor before the top-12 cutoff

issues.title: Briefing precision: a relevance floor before the top-12 cutoff, measured
issues.body:
## Why

The briefing always fills its twelve slots. The search is an OR of the task's subject words, ranked by BM25, cut at the limit, with no floor on how well a record matched. On a short or generic prompt that means twelve records chosen by one shared word. From the probe in PR #256 (`evals/results/probe-rephrase-20261021.txt`, six prompts taken verbatim from one session, this repo's interests):

| prompt | records returned | matched one word only | the word |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| "this seems like a major point to scrutinize" | 12 | 12 | point, major |
| "what about the org knowledge idea, is that a niche?" | 10 | 10 | org |
| "give me a doc for that too" | 12 | 12 | give, doc |
| "how do we come up with a good plan for governing github copilot and mcp" | 12 | 10 | plan, governing, come |

Those twelve arrive in the agent's context as imperatives under "Do this", including a remote-sensing compositing rule for the word "point". The hook output for the first prompt is about 8,800 characters, roughly 2,200 tokens, on every such prompt. This is the recorded defect "ranking works, filtering doesn't" in its remaining form: the cutoff bounded the count, not the relevance.

## What to do

Add a relevance floor before the cutoff, and report what it removed:

- A record is briefed only if it matches **two or more** of the task's subject words, or one word when the task has only one. On the probe this keeps 0, 4, 0, 0, 2 and 3 of the twelve for the six prompts above, and keeps **all eight** authored eval tasks' governing records (each matches 2 to 10 words). A rarity-based floor (a word in at most 3% of the store) was also tried and loses two of the eight, so it is the wrong shape.
- When the floor empties the briefing, say so in the hook line: "0 relevant lessons; 12 weak matches trimmed" is a different fact from "0 lessons in the store", and both differ from silence.
- `okl check --format json` gains the matched-word count per record and the number trimmed by the floor, so the exposure log can keep it.

## Measure before merging

`evals/preflight.py` must stay green (it already asserts each task's record is present). Re-run `evals/probe_rephrase.py` and commit the receipt beside the one in PR #256; the floor must not change any "yes" in its recall table. Then one A/B on the §4m instrument, since a shorter briefing is also a cheaper one and #234 is already measuring briefing size.

title: okl check --path: the lessons that govern a file, before it is read or edited (#94)
lesson_text:
[remote-path-test-through-client] Defect · A remote path tested only by posting to the service never exercises the client that calls it
symptom: a client feature works locally and its service endpoint passes its own tests, but every real call through the client fails (a 422 on a null the client sends, a 404 on an id the client URL-encodes)
fix: test every remote path through the real client: route its HTTP library to the in-process app (patch urlopen to a TestClient) so the client's encoding, defaults and error mapping meet the server's validation; keep one such test per endpoint the client calls, and give it an input the client filters or trims before sending, down to empty
body: cause: okl R1's service tests posted JSON straight to the app, and the client was only ever tested in local mode. Two defects lived in the gap: the MCP tool sent replace=null, which the typed service model refuses, so every record over a service failed; and GET /node/{id} never matched an id holding a slash the client had encoded. Both reviewers of R1 found them; no test could have.

title: Make the drift gate say when it checked nothing, instead of passing

issues.title: drift --gate passes against an empty store, checking nothing
issues.body:
`okl drift --gate` exits 0 when the store it reads is empty (`src/okl/cli.py`, `cmd_drift`: it returns 1 only when `hits and args.gate`).

In CI without `OKL_SERVICE_URL`, `drift` reads the repo-local `.okl/`, which `okl init` gitignores. So the store is empty, there are no hits, and the gate passes having checked nothing. `check` already refuses to report clean on an empty or unconfigured store; `drift --gate` should fail closed the same way, since "no drift" and "nothing was checked" look identical to the PR author.

Found in emeraldleaf-dev, which removed its drift workflow for this reason (see its AGENTS.md, "The knowledge layer").

**Suggested fix:** under `--gate`, exit non-zero when the store holds no records for the repo (or none that declare `files`), with a message naming the cause. Or document that the workflow must run `okl seed` first, and have `okl init`'s generated workflow do so.

Collapsing 2 into 0 is the silence-as-safety failure the whole tool exists to prevent, and collapsing it into 1 makes a misconfiguration look like a finding.

title: Retire a lesson with a reason: wrong, replaced or obsolete (okl review R2)
lesson_text:
[remote-timeout-not-a-deadline] Defect · A per-socket timeout is not a deadline, and a failure after the request was sent is not 'not written'
symptom: a fail-closed hook against a stalled shared service runs past its host's time limit (Claude Code cancels a UserPromptSubmit hook at 30 s and lets the prompt through unbriefed), or a write reported as lost turns up stored twice after the user retries
fix: budget the caller's worst case per address and per read (or set a real deadline around the whole call), and stop retrying a try that failed slowly, since that is an outage rather than a transient; catch the post-send errors (OSError, http.client.HTTPException) after URLError and fail closed on them; for a write, say 'maybe recorded' (search before retrying, or retry idempotently with the same id), never 'not recorded', and test the retry you call safe: an identical second call must write nothing new; keep a test that reads the retry loop's numbers from the shipped hook and asserts the worst case stays under the host's limit
body: cause: Python urllib's timeout applies to each connect attempt, once per address the host resolves to, and to each socket read; it is not a limit on the whole call, and a DNS lookup is not covered at all. urllib wraps connect and send failures in URLError, but failures while reading the reply escape raw: TimeoutError, ConnectionResetError, RemoteDisconnected, BadStatusLine, IncompleteRead. okl's client caught only HTTPError and URLError, so a stalled service crashed okl check with a traceback, and the hook's three 10 s tries took 31.6 s (okl #156, review R10). Two black-holed addresses still took 31.5 s at 5 s a try. Also: bash SECONDS counts whole seconds, so a '-ge N' elapsed check only guarantees a try under N-1 s reads as quick.

lesson_redactions.why: cites PR #163's retry test, this task's own fix

defect: okl_retire says a retry is safe, but every retry appends another retirement row.

title: The reranker's model lives under the cache home, not the system temp directory
lesson_text:
[fastembed-cache-in-tmpdir] Rule · fastembed keeps its models in the system temp directory by default, so a cached model can vanish and a model sweep must spare the ones in use
symptom: a tool that loaded its ONNX model offline yesterday says the model is not cached today; or the temp directory holds gigabytes of model blobs nobody remembers downloading
fix: when a model must stay available offline, pass an explicit cache_dir under the user's cache home (or set FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH) rather than relying on the temp dir; when sweeping the cache, keep only the blobs the models in use reference: each model dir's symlinks resolve to its blobs, and the shared blobs/ tree is hashed files under two-character directories, so delete files, never directories, and prune empty dirs after
body: cause: fastembed's default cache_dir is tempfile.gettempdir()/fastembed_cache (on macOS a per-user /var/folders/.../T path that the system prunes). okl's reranker spike left 2.7 GB of ONNX blobs there (2026-10-24); the shipped reranker lives in the same tree, and macOS can evict it, after which okl check --rerank reports the model as not cached until okl embed runs online again.
defect: None: the reranker already loads with cache_dir under the user's cache home.
control_mutation: in src/okl/rerank.py, drop cache_dir=str(hub.model_cache_dir()) from the TextCrossEncoder(...) call: the grader fails

title: harness: refuse a run whose working tree moved
lesson_text:
[harness-reads-a-moving-working-tree] Defect · An eval run that renders from the working tree must own it: a branch switch mid-run changes the code behind half the samples and the commit the receipt names
symptom: a receipt's okl_commit names a branch other than the one the run was started on, or the harness log's first line and the receipt disagree about HEAD; samples late in a run were produced by code the pre-registration never described
fix: run the harness from a dedicated git worktree pinned to the pre-registered commit, never from the tree other work uses; have the harness record HEAD at start, re-read it before writing the receipt, and when they differ stamp both and set usable=false; until that lands, do not switch branches in a checkout with a run in progress
body: cause: ab_harness runs the briefed arm as 'python -m okl' against src/ in the checkout and stamps okl_commit from the tree's HEAD when it writes the receipt, at the end. On 2026-10-22 the tree was switched from the symptom-rule branch (acdcb99) to the relevance-floor branch during a 25-minute run to answer a review; the receipt (ab-20261022-0455) names b54e075 and the later samples were briefed by code with the floor. The briefings were identical by §4n's identity test, so the result survived, but only by argument.
defect: None: the harness already records HEAD at the start, re-reads it before the receipt, and marks a run whose tree moved not usable.

title: Safe install and uninstall: fingerprinted files, okl init --uninstall, OKL_DISABLED_HOOKS

issues.title: Safe install and uninstall: fingerprinted okl files, okl init --uninstall, OKL_DISABLED_HOOKS
issues.body:
## Problem
- `okl init` overwrites `.claude/hooks/*.sh` on every run (`_install_claude_wiring`): a local edit is silently lost. That breaks the recorded rule that anything okl writes into someone else's repo is idempotent and non-clobbering.
- There is no uninstall. Removing okl means hand-editing `.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json` and deleting files, next to other tools' hooks (claude-mem, agentmemory, ECC, beads — see #40).
- There is no switch to turn one hook off while keeping the other, e.g. the Stop question when another tool's Stop hooks already run (#40).

ECC does this well (hook IDs + fingerprints, surgical uninstall, `ECC_DISABLED_HOOKS`); this is the okl-sized version.

## Design
1. **Self-verifying fingerprint.** Each okl-owned file (both hooks, the CI workflow) carries `# okl-fingerprint: sha256:<hash of the rest of the file>`. Matching hash = an unmodified okl file of *any* version → safe to upgrade or remove. Mismatch = edited → kept, reported, `--force` to replace. No local state, so it works for a teammate who cloned the repo. A test fails with the correct value when a fingerprint is stale.
2. **`okl init` stops clobbering.** It upgrades unmodified okl files, installs missing ones, and keeps edited ones with a warning.
3. **`okl init --uninstall [--dry-run]`.** Removes okl's exact hook entries from settings (dropping empty groups/events), the `okl` MCP entry if it is exactly what okl wrote, and fingerprint-matching files. Never touches `.okl/` (the store is user data). Prints what it kept and why.
4. **`OKL_DISABLED_HOOKS=briefing,encode`.** Honoured by the hook scripts; each exits 0 when named.

lesson_text:
[n_58119d0a63d9] Rule · Init must wire, not instruct — every 'now copy X / add Y to config' printout is a surface nobody runs
symptom: an installer prints manual follow-up steps (register this hook, copy this workflow, add to settings)
fix: make init perform each registration itself, idempotent and non-clobbering; warn loudly only for what it truly cannot do (e.g. no git repo -> drift disabled)
body: cause: the installer stops where the mechanical work gets fiddly (JSON merging, no-clobber checks), so the last mile becomes a printed TODO — and the component it gates (hooks, CI verifier, MCP tools) silently never runs. okl init had four of these at once: hooks installed but unregistered in settings.json, a CI workflow that was a copy instruction, verify steps that were echo placeholders, and an MCP registration hint. The fix is always the same shape: do the merge idempotently (preserve existing config, never duplicate, never clobber), and reserve printed output for genuinely human decisions.
defect: None: init registers its hook settings itself, idempotently, and uninstall removes exactly them.
control_mutation: in _merge_hook_settings, wanted = [...] becomes wanted = []: the grader fails
